engineChanges.change: All Leander values are unverified assumptions; require user to confirm zoning district, plat building lines and adopted code edition before finalizing
SFU Single-Family Urban (composite, e.g. SFU-2-B): use front 20 / side 5 / street side 15 / rear 10 ft as provisional defaults (unverified)
Use IECC Climate Zone 2A prescriptive envelope for the adopted IECC edition
Flag PE-sealed engineered slab (expansive clay east of I-35 / variable limestone and clay in the west)

Check the TCEQ Edwards Aquifer map: lots on the recharge zone (and some in the contributing/transition zones) fall under 30 TAC Chapter 213; regulated development needs an approved Water Pollution Abatement Plan, usually done at subdivision level. Leander is largely in the contributing zone, with some recharge zone in the south/west.
Require tree survey; avoid heritage-tree critical root zones (>= ~26 in DBH) or add mitigation cost
Add Leander water, wastewater and roadway impact fees (amounts not retrieved; Leander is believed to collect roadway impact fees)
Most new homes are in PUDs/MUDs or HOA subdivisions - plat building lines, PUD standards and deed restrictions may override district setbacks and add masonry rules

plainLanguage: This Leander file is unverified - our research tools were unavailable, so treat every number as a placeholder. Leander uses an unusual 'composite' zoning code: a zoning label like SFU-2-B combines the home type, the lot standards and the look of the house. Many new neighborhoods are planned developments with their own rules. Expect water, sewer and road impact fees. Big trees are protected, and some areas are over the Edwards Aquifer.
